source.label: The Economist · Big Mac index (course data pack)
filters: 45 supplied observations from 2000-04-01 through 2026-07-01. No new market data fetched.

evidenceFlow.title: Read supplied course CSV
evidenceFlow.detail: bigmac.csv, 2,056 rows, one country or area per observation date. Data supplied in the MSIN0167 Week 6 pack.

evidenceFlow.title: Convert values to percentages
evidenceFlow.detail: Multiply each raw and GDP-adjusted fraction by 100; preserve missing adjusted estimates as null. Join countries by iso_a3.

metricDefinitions.label: Raw valuation (%)
metricDefinitions.definition: The supplied raw index × 100, relative to the selected base currency. Positive means a more expensive Big Mac relative to the base; negative means cheaper.

metricDefinitions.label: GDP-adjusted valuation (%)
metricDefinitions.definition: The supplied GDP-adjusted index × 100. Adjustment allows for differences in GDP per person. Missing estimates remain unavailable.

metricDefinitions.label: Change (pp)
metricDefinitions.definition: End-reading valuation minus start-reading valuation for the same country and measure, in percentage points. Both values must exist.

metricDefinitions.label: Median absolute valuation gap
metricDefinitions.definition: Median absolute valuation across countries with both raw and GDP-adjusted estimates, excluding the selected base country.

caveats: A simple purchasing-power comparison, not an exact estimate of currency mispricing.
Coverage varies by date. Lebanon and Venezuela have no adjusted estimates in July 2026.
Dates are not evenly spaced; historical lines use actual calendar dates.
The displayed country name can vary historically; ISO identity is used for joins.

methods.code: df = pd.read_csv('bigmac.csv'); assert not df.duplicated(['date','iso_a3']).any(); # Keep date, ISO identity, country name, dollar price and raw/adjusted fields. Multiply each fraction by 100 and keep missing values null.

// Snapshot: filter rows by exact selected date; exclude the selected base country for comparisons. Compute median(abs(raw)) and median(abs(adjusted)) on the same rows with both values. History uses actual date positions. Heatmap uses the last supplied observation in each calendar year. Change = end - start for a one-to-one ISO join with both non-missing values; display in percentage points.
